rics.meaning: Federal budget deficit (or surplus) — outlays minus receipts on a unified-budget basis. Released monthly by Treasury's Monthly Treasury Statement, fiscal year basis (Oct-Sep).
rics.how_to_use: The headline fiscal print. Cyclical: widens in recessions (auto stabilizers), narrows in expansions. Recent run rate ~$1.5-2T deficit annually post-COVID, structurally elevated relative to pre-2020. Watch primary deficit (excl interest) for underlying fiscal stance.

rics.description: Federal Government total surplus or deficit
rics.meaning: Federal government total surplus or deficit — annual/fiscal-year aggregate, complementary to the monthly aUSGDEFAA series. Same conceptual measure at lower frequency.
rics.how_to_use: Use the monthly series (aUSGDEFAA) for high-frequency tracking; use this annual aggregate for historical comparison. Compare to GDP for the deficit-to-GDP ratio, the standard sustainability metric (~5-7% in recent years).

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: administration of justice — DOJ, FBI, federal courts, immigration enforcement, prisons. ~$70B annually.
rics.how_to_use: Discretionary spending. Watch for immigration-enforcement appropriations (DHS budget surge under Trump 2017+ and 2025+). Smaller share of total but politically watched.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays — agriculture (farm subsidies, USDA).
rics.how_to_use: Highly variable: farm bill cycle and price-support programs swing the line item.

rics.description: Federal outlays, commerce and housing credit
rics.meaning: Federal outlays — commerce and housing credit.
rics.how_to_use: Includes Fannie/Freddie support, SBA. Surged in COVID (PPP loans).

rics.description: Federal outlays, community and regional development
rics.meaning: Federal outlays: community and regional development — HUD community-development block grants, EDA programs, rural development. ~$40B annually.
rics.how_to_use: Small discretionary category. Includes urban-renewal grants and rural infrastructure funding. Watch for major program changes (CDBG zeroed in some Trump budgets, restored in others).

rics.description: Federal outlays, education, training, empl & social serv
rics.meaning: Federal outlays — education, training, employment & social services.
rics.how_to_use: Department of Education + DOL. Student-loan-related outlays move this materially.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays — energy (DOE).
rics.how_to_use: ~1% of outlays. Includes nuclear weapons stewardship via NNSA.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: general government — Treasury, GSA, OPM, central agencies. The 'overhead' of running the federal government.
rics.how_to_use: Stable around $30-40B. Useful for tracking federal-workforce size; rises when Congress funds federal pay raises.

rics.description: Federal outlays, general science, space and technology
rics.meaning: Federal outlays: general science, space and technology — NASA, NSF, basic research. ~$45B annually.
rics.how_to_use: Includes NASA (~$25B). NSF and DOE basic research split the rest. Track for science-policy debates and Mars-mission/Artemis funding.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: health (excluding Medicare) — Medicaid, NIH, CDC, CHIP, public health. ~$700B annually combined.
rics.how_to_use: Medicaid is the dominant component (~$600B federal share, with state matches adding more). Growth driven by ACA expansion, demographic aging, and per-enrollee medical-cost inflation. ACA Medicaid expansion in 41 states drove sustained growth post-2014.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays — income security (unemployment, SNAP, housing assistance).
rics.how_to_use: Counter-cyclical: spikes in recessions. The COVID UI surge dominated 2020-21.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: net interest — interest paid on federal debt minus interest received. Fastest-growing major category as debt level meets higher rates.
rics.how_to_use: Has crossed $1T annually post-2024, exceeding defense outlays. Trajectory determined by both debt growth (deficits) and average rate on debt (refinancing higher-coupon debt). Major fiscal sustainability concern; CBO projects net interest reaching 4% of GDP by 2034.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: international affairs — State Department, USAID, foreign aid, embassies. ~$70B annually.
rics.how_to_use: ~1% of federal budget. Includes military aid (Israel, Ukraine, Egypt, Jordan), economic aid, multilateral commitments. Variable: surges during major foreign aid (Ukraine 2022-25) or pandemic response.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: Medicare — health insurance for 65+ population (~65M beneficiaries). Second-largest federal outlay, ~$1T and growing fastest among major categories due to aging + medical-cost inflation.
rics.how_to_use: Hospital Insurance (Part A) trust fund projected insolvent ~2031. Total Medicare growth ~6%/year vs ~4% economic growth — structural fiscal stress. Watch alongside Medicaid (state-level partner program) for total federal health-care fiscal exposure.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: national defense — DOD plus military assistance, atomic energy defense activities. ~$850B annually, ~13% of total federal outlays.
rics.how_to_use: Has fallen from ~5% of GDP in 2010 to ~3% in 2024 as percent of GDP, even as nominal level rose. Discretionary spending (subject to annual appropriations) — the largest target for budget negotiations. Geopolitical events (Ukraine, Middle East) have driven supplemental requests.

rics.description: Federal outlays, natural resources and environment
rics.meaning: Federal outlays: natural resources and environment — EPA, Interior, USFS, USGS. ~$45B annually.
rics.how_to_use: Includes federal lands management (BLM, USFS), national parks, EPA enforcement. Watch for environmental-policy shifts; major budget changes often tied to administration changes.

rics.meaning: Federal outlays: Social Security — retirement and survivor benefits to ~67M beneficiaries. Largest single federal outlay category, ~$1.4T annually and growing with demographics.
rics.how_to_use: Mandatory spending — paid by formula not appropriations. Trust Fund projected to be insolvent by ~2034 absent legislation; would trigger automatic ~20% benefit cut. Track demographic profile (boomer retirement wave continues through 2034).

rics.meaning: Federal government outlays (total) — Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, defense, interest on debt, all other discretionary + mandatory programs. Released monthly by Treasury.
rics.how_to_use: Mandatory + interest now ~75% of outlays — limited room for discretionary cuts. Net interest outlays passing $1T annually, growing fastest. Track interest-as-share-of-revenues for fiscal-sustainability stress signal (now ~20%, doubled vs 2010s).

rics.meaning: Federal outlays — transportation (DOT, FAA, highway trust fund).
rics.how_to_use: Infrastructure spending tracked here. IIJA boost showing through.

rics.meaning: Undistributed offsetting receipts — negative line (mineral leases, employer share of pension contributions).
rics.how_to_use: Treated as negative outlay in budget accounting. Don't include in 'spending share' analysis.

rics.meaning: Federal government receipts (revenues) — individual income taxes, corporate income taxes, payroll taxes, customs duties, excise taxes. Released monthly by Treasury.
rics.how_to_use: Individual income tax is ~50%, payroll tax ~35%, corporate ~10%. Cyclical: rises with GDP and labor income. April spike from individual tax filings; December peak from corporate quarterly estimated payments. Tariff-policy changes show up in customs duties (small share).

rics.description: GOVERNMENT BUDGET OUTLAYS FOR VETERANS BENEFITS
rics.meaning: Federal outlays — veterans benefits.
rics.how_to_use: Growing line as post-9/11 cohort ages and benefits expand (PACT Act).

rics.meaning: Central government deficit/surplus, standardized — OECD-comparable framing of US federal budget balance. Includes only central-government level (excludes state and local).
rics.how_to_use: Use for cross-country fiscal-position comparisons. US-domestic analysts use unified-budget aUSGDEFAA. The central-government framing aligns with IMF Article IV and OECD reporting.

rics.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, month on month, Standardized, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Central government balance MoM absolute change.
rics.how_to_use: Use YoY for trend.

rics.description: Central government Deficit/Surplus, year on year, Standardized, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Central government balance YoY absolute change.
rics.how_to_use: Cleaner trend; strips monthly tax-timing noise.

rics.meaning: Federal net outlays — outlays minus offsetting receipts (user fees, royalties on federal lands, mineral leases). The 'net spending' figure used in budget arithmetic.
rics.how_to_use: Smaller than gross outlays by ~$200B (offsetting receipts). Use for budget-arithmetic consistency; gross outlays (aUSFOUTL) is the more commonly cited measure.

rics.meaning: Federal receipts (alternative framing) — companion to aUSFEDREC at potentially different release vintage.
rics.how_to_use: Cross-check series. Use whichever is fresher. The OMB and Treasury release the same data with slight timing differences.

rics.description: Federal surplus/deficit as percent of GDP
rics.meaning: Federal surplus/deficit as % of GDP — the standard fiscal-stance gauge.
rics.how_to_use: >5% deficit during expansion is highly unusual and signals limited fiscal room for the next recession. Compare to historical norm (~2-3% during expansions). Fiscal projections (CBO baseline) suggest persistence above 5%.
